---
title: "Toy Fixture Spike"
date: 2026-08-19
---

**Verdict: GO.** A fully self-contained JHEEM model — no data managers, no NAS, no `jheem_analyses` — compiles, registers, and **runs in 0.37 seconds** with sane dynamics (population grows at fertility-minus-mortality; incidence grows exponentially from seeded infections). The full script is at the bottom; it is the seed of the package fixture, runnable `@examples`, and the quickstart vignette ([D-008](decisions.qmd)).

## The minimal-model recipe

Discovered by error-driven iteration (jheem2's validation messages are genuinely good — most errors said exactly what was missing):

1. `create.jheem.specification` formally requires only `version`, `iteration`, `description`, `start.year` — and `start.year` must be in **[1800, 1980]**.
2. The compiler requires exactly four dynamics registrations, and enumerates all of them in one error: `register.mortality`, `register.natality`, `register.transmission`, `register.initial.population`.
3. Scalar constants are accepted almost everywhere: rates, fertility, susceptibility, proportions can all be plain numbers or references to scalar quantities.
4. **At least one dynamic outcome** must be tracked (built-in dynamic quantities: `population`, `mortality`, `births`, `incidence` and variants, `remission`).
5. **At least one model element** (with a functional form) must be registered; `create.static.functional.form(value=..., link=...)` is the simplest.
6. Paired from/to dimensions (contact mixing, birth proportions) are introduced with the **subset idiom**: a scalar base `register.model.quantity` plus `register.model.quantity.subset` whose `applies.to` uses `<dim>.from` / `<dim>.to` names. Literal arrays with those dimnames are not accepted.
7. Quantities that must span model dimensions (initial population needs `age` × `sex`) also use the subset idiom — see bug 3 below for why literal arrays fail.
8. Age compartment labels are auto-formatted from `age.endpoints` (e.g., `"0-49 years"`, `"50+ years"`); error messages state the expected labels.
9. Population as a gettable outcome follows the EHE pattern: a `track.point.outcome` over `expression(uninfected + infected)` (built-in state quantities), wrapped in a `track.integrated.outcome`.
10. `engine$run()` requires a **named** numeric parameter vector; an empty named vector works when the spec defines no sampleable parameters. Any real location code works (`C.12580` used) since nothing pulls location data.

## Engine bugs found in empty and minimal cases

| # | Symptom | Cause | Status |
|---|---------|-------|--------|
| 1 | `invalid subscript type 'list'` at engine creation | Zero dynamic outcomes → `sapply` over empty vector returns `list()`, used as a subscript (`R/JHEEM_kernel.R` ~line 289) | **Fixed on `dev`** (2026-08-19, `90b68ad`): `vapply` with typed FUN.VALUE; zero-outcome specs now run. Toy fingerprint verified identical before/after |
| 2 | `invalid argument type` at run | Zero model elements → empty-`sapply` `list()` assigned into a logical vector silently coerces it to a list (`R/JHEEM_engine.R` ~line 3411) | **Fixed on `dev`** (same commit); zero-element specs now run |
| 3 | `missing required dimensions` at run for an array-valued quantity | A literal array value **passes compile-time dimname validation** but its dims are lost by the run-time dimname resolution — the two paths disagree | **Open.** Touches live dimname-resolution paths; deferred until the fixture-based test net exists ([D-001](decisions.qmd)). Workaround: the subset idiom |

Also noted (quirk, not crash): `track.dynamic.outcome` of the `population` dynamic quantity compiles and runs but extracts as all-zero; the point+integrated pattern (recipe step 9) is what real specs use.

## Verified behavior

```
run wall time: 0.37 s
population by year (1970, 1990, 2010): 4024, 4915, 6003
incidence  by year (1971, 1990, 2010): 0.46, 2.51, 14.49
```

Initial population is 4,000 (1,000 × 2 ages × 2 sexes); growth matches fertility 0.02 vs mortality 0.01; incidence grows from 4 seeded undiagnosed infections through the uniform-mixing transmission machinery.

## The working script

```r
library(jheem2)

spec = create.jheem.specification(
    version = "toy",
    iteration = "1",
    description = "Minimal self-contained toy model for tests and examples",
    start.year = 1970,
    age.endpoints = c(0, 50, Inf),
    compartments.for.infected.and.uninfected = list(
        location = "location",
        age = "all.ages",
        sex = c("female", "male")
    ),
    compartments.for.infected.only = list(
        continuum = c("undiagnosed", "diagnosed")
    ))

# Mortality: flat rate for everyone
register.model.quantity(spec, name = "toy.mortality.rate", value = 0.01)
register.mortality(spec,
                   groups = c("infected", "uninfected"),
                   mortality.rate.value = "toy.mortality.rate")

# Natality: flat fertility; births are uninfected, into age group 1, 50/50 sex
register.model.quantity(spec, name = "toy.fertility.rate", value = 0.02)
register.model.quantity(spec, name = "toy.birth.proportions", value = 0)
register.model.quantity.subset(spec, name = "toy.birth.proportions",
                               applies.to = list(sex.to = c("female", "male")),
                               value = 0.5)
register.natality(spec,
                  parent.groups = c("infected", "uninfected"),
                  child.groups = "uninfected",
                  fertility.rate.value = "toy.fertility.rate",
                  birth.proportions.value = "toy.birth.proportions",
                  all.births.into.compartments = list(age = 1))

# One model element with a functional form (required; also the calibration hook)
register.model.element(spec,
                       name = "transmission.rate",
                       scale = "rate",
                       functional.form = create.static.functional.form(value = 0.1, link = "log"))

# Transmission: uniform sex mixing, constant susceptibility,
# all new infections start undiagnosed
register.model.quantity(spec, name = "toy.contact", value = 0)
register.model.quantity.subset(spec, name = "toy.contact",
                               applies.to = list(sex.from = c("female", "male"),
                                                 sex.to = c("female", "male")),
                               value = 0.5)
register.model.quantity(spec, name = "toy.susceptibility", value = 1)
register.model.quantity(spec, name = "toy.new.infection.proportions", value = 1)
register.transmission(spec,
                      contact.value = "toy.contact",
                      susceptibility.value = "toy.susceptibility",
                      transmissibility.value = "transmission.rate",
                      new.infection.proportions.value = "toy.new.infection.proportions",
                      new.infections.applies.to = list(continuum = "undiagnosed"))

# Initial population: 1000 uninfected per age x sex stratum,
# 1 seeded undiagnosed infection per stratum
register.model.quantity(spec, name = "toy.init.uninfected", value = 0)
register.model.quantity.subset(spec, name = "toy.init.uninfected",
                               applies.to = list(age = c("0-49 years", "50+ years"),
                                                 sex = c("female", "male")),
                               value = 1000)
register.initial.population(spec, group = "uninfected", value = "toy.init.uninfected")
register.model.quantity(spec, name = "init.infected", value = 0)
register.model.quantity.subset(spec, name = "init.infected",
                               applies.to = list(continuum = "undiagnosed",
                                                 age = c("0-49 years", "50+ years"),
                                                 sex = c("female", "male")),
                               value = 1)
register.initial.population(spec, group = "infected", value = "init.infected")

# Outcomes: incidence (dynamic) + population (point outcome, integrated)
track.dynamic.outcome(spec,
                      name = "incidence",
                      outcome.metadata = create.outcome.metadata(
                          display.name = "Incidence",
                          description = "New infections in the past year",
                          scale = "non.negative.number",
                          axis.name = "Infections",
                          units = "infections",
                          singular.unit = "infection"),
                      dynamic.quantity.name = "incidence",
                      keep.dimensions = c("location", "age", "sex"))

track.point.outcome(spec,
                    "point.population",
                    scale = "non.negative.number",
                    value = expression(uninfected + infected),
                    keep.dimensions = c("location", "age", "sex"),
                    outcome.metadata = create.outcome.metadata(
                        display.name = "Point population",
                        description = "Population at a point in time",
                        scale = "non.negative.number",
                        axis.name = "People",
                        units = "people",
                        singular.unit = "person"))

track.integrated.outcome(spec,
                         name = "population",
                         outcome.metadata = create.outcome.metadata(
                             display.name = "Population",
                             description = "Total population over the year",
                             scale = "non.negative.number",
                             axis.name = "People",
                             units = "people",
                             singular.unit = "person"),
                         value.to.integrate = "point.population",
                         keep.dimensions = c("location", "age", "sex"))

register.model.specification(spec)

engine = create.jheem.engine("toy", "C.12580", end.year = 2010)
sim = engine$run(setNames(numeric(0), character(0)))

sim$get("population", year = c(1970, 1990, 2010))
sim$get("incidence", year = c(1971, 1990, 2010))
```
